subject.title: Beta-tagged update can leave official external plugins on latest instead of the requested beta tag

question: For an explicit exact beta core update, should trusted official external plugins converge to that same exact version, and should missing or invalid matching plugin artifacts warn or fail the update?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally allow beta-channel fallback, but the reported explicit-tag path needs a product choice before automation can safely change upgrade semantics.

options.title: Exact match with warning
options.body: Target official npm plugins at the installed core beta version when available, and emit structured post-update warnings without failing when a matching artifact is unavailable or invalid.

options.title: Exact match fail-closed
options.body: Require matching official plugin artifacts for explicit beta core updates and fail the post-core update when any active trusted official plugin cannot align.

options.title: Keep current fallback
options.body: Keep beta plugin convergence on channel/default fallback semantics and document that explicit core tags do not imply plugin exact-version alignment.

recommendation.title: Exact match with warning
recommendation.body: Target official npm plugins at the installed core beta version when available, and emit structured post-update warnings without failing when a matching artifact is unavailable or invalid.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to the original update-channel/plugin sync behavior and adjacent post-core update policy decisions.
